slot.brief: evaluate a definite rational/trig integral with the Weierstrass substitution t = tan(x/2), changing limits accordingly

verdicts.working: With t = tan(x/2), the integral becomes ∫₀∞ dt/(t²+t+1) = (2/√3)[arctan((2t+1)/√3)]₀∞ = 2π/(3√3).

working:
Using $\int_0^\pi f(\sin x)dx = 2\int_0^{\pi/2} f(\sin x)dx$, we get $I = 2\int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{dx}{2+\sin x}$.
Substitute $t = \tan\frac{x}{2}$: $x=0 \Rightarrow t=0$, $x=\frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow t=1$, $dx = \frac{2}{1+t^2}dt$, $\sin x = \frac{2t}{1+t^2}$.
Then $2+\sin x = 2 + \frac{2t}{1+t^2} = \frac{2(t^2+t+1)}{1+t^2}$.
The integrand becomes $\frac{1}{2+\sin x}dx = \frac{1}{\frac{2(t^2+t+1)}{1+t^2}} \cdot \frac{2}{1+t^2}dt = \frac{1}{t^2+t+1}dt$.
So $I = 2\int_0^1 \frac{dt}{t^2+t+1} = 2\int_0^1 \frac{dt}{(t+\frac12)^2 + \frac34}$.
$= 2 \cdot \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\left[\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{2t+1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\right]_0^1 = \frac{4}{\sqrt{3}}\left(\frac{\pi}{3} - \frac{\pi}{6}\right) = \frac{4}{\sqrt{3}} \cdot \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{2\pi}{3\sqrt{3}}$.

Independent check: With t = tan(x/2), the integral becomes ∫₀∞ dt/(t²+t+1) = (2/√3)[arctan((2t+1)/√3)]₀∞ = 2π/(3√3).
solution:
Using symmetry, $I=2\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{dx}{2+\sin x}$. Let $t=\tan\frac{x}{2}$; then $dx=\frac{2\,dt}{1+t^2}$ and $\sin x=\frac{2t}{1+t^2}$, with limits $0$ and $1$.
$$I=2\int_0^1\frac{dt}{t^2+t+1}=\frac{4}{\sqrt3}\left[\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{2t+1}{\sqrt3}\right)\right]_0^1=\frac{2\pi}{3\sqrt3}.$$
